organizations.active_dates: Published under Home News names during Hugh N. Boyd's documented staff tenure; exact corporate-name chronology requires further normalization review
organizations.normalization_notes: The historical names printed by the reviewed sources are preserved. The project does not silently substitute the modern successor newspaper or merge the newspaper with later broadcasting subsidiaries.

affiliations.date_precision: The local history sequences his newspaper work after his studies and before Army/OSS service during World War II; the Congressional Record history says he later completed 44 years as a staff member, but neither source supplies exact prewar start or military-leave dates
affiliations.research_notes: The uncommon exact full name, newspaper chronology, and explicit Army/OSS statement support a high-confidence identity. The newspaper is the best-supported last civilian employer before wartime service, but no reviewed source proves it was the immediate affiliation before a distinct OSS transfer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Hugh N. Boyd is a high-confidence match to the New Brunswick newspaperman documented as serving with the Army in Europe as part of OSS.
claims.evidence_excerpt: serve in the Army in Europe as part of the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A sourced local-history account identifies the exact uncommon name, sequences his Home News work before wartime Army/OSS service, and describes his postwar return; an independent federal reprint documents his long Home News staff tenure.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact uncommon full name and middle initial, explicit OSS statement, New Brunswick newspaper chronology, and independent long-tenure evidence provide multiple corroborating identifiers beyond the name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The account explicitly places newspaper work before World War II Army/OSS service and postwar advancement afterward, but does not supply OSS entry dates.
claims.match_notes: The index supplies no rank or service identifier. The match remains high confidence rather than confirmed pending Box 73 personnel-file review.

claims.claim_text: The Home News in New Brunswick is the best-supported last civilian employer for Hugh N. Boyd before his wartime Army/OSS service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: joined the paper, first in the business department and then as a reporter
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The local-history account sequences Boyd's work at the paper before his wartime Army/OSS service; the Congressional Record reprints an institutional history documenting 44 years on the Home News staff.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity based on the exact uncommon name, explicit OSS connection, and matching newspaper chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as pre-service employment. Exact start, military-leave, and OSS-entry dates are unavailable, so the claim is not labeled explicit immediate.
claims.match_notes: Published as last civilian employment, not as proof that the newspaper immediately preceded a separate OSS transfer. The Army is not mislabeled as a civilian employer.
